C-ATTEMPT-LOG.IntentSummary:
Record every attempt rather than only outcomes, bound churn at two, and escalate to replan rather than abort — per D6's attempt half and D9.
Authored before execution, per A17.3. Phase 3's bundle carried a spec alone and its plan was written retrospectively as a recorded exception; this one is not an exception.
Task order is not a preference. T-001 fixes the fold, because at 235f0f8 the fold destroys event payload and reports success while doing it (A18.2, correction 31). Every later task writes payload. Building them first would write evidence into a shredder and every test asserting on loose files would pass while the ledger kept nothing.

T-001.Title: Fold preserves payload, and verify compares instead of counting

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: buildEpochNode carries event attributes and children into the ledger; the fold's verify step compares written payload against the loose events; a fold that drops a field fails its own verify and leaves every loose file on disk, proven by injection rather than by a passing happy path. The A18.2 probe re-run verbatim. The A7.2 both-directions table for the verify boundary. The no-op filter at :344 removed.

T-002.Title: Attempt events with allocated ids, three-valued outcome, and derived ordinal

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Attempts are run events carrying D2's allocated id — no persisted ordinal, no timestamp, no second identity. The outcome is pass, fail, or absent, reusing AbsenceValue; a verification that could not run produces a verification-unavailable event rather than an attempt. Presence is asserted against the FOLDED ledger, never against loose files.

T-003.Title: Dumb counter, escalation to paused-pending-approval, and one exhaustive kind-to-state map

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: The budget counts attempt events and inspects nothing; 2 is a named constant with D9's "judgment, not derived" note. Two different signatures still exhaust it; two verification-unavailable events do not, and both survive the fold. Exhaustion transitions to paused-pending-approval and surfaces both signatures without claiming failure. Both kind-to-state ternaries (:235-236 and :465) become one exhaustive map with an explicit unknown-kind branch, proven by dropping the cursor and re-deriving from the ledger. The A5.4 drop-site inventory for CursorState, re-measured.

T-004.Title: Parse the written cursor state, and classify flakes from recorded evidence

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: The unchecked cast at :438 becomes a parse against the widened union; an unrecognized value takes the existing degradation path and cursor show still answers while lint still reports. Flake classification reads write evidence snapshotted onto each attempt event and issues no git call at report time, with three fixtures giving three verdicts: flaky, normal retry, and unable-to-determine when the evidence was unavailable.

T-005.Title: Execute skill states the budget and escalation rule, mirrored

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: ngrace-execute/SKILL.md states when an attempt is recorded, what exhaustion does, and that escalation is a pause awaiting a decision rather than a failure — one or two sentences, restating no codes the binary emits. The packaged mirror is byte-identical in the same commit. Line and token delta reported. Invariant 5 demonstrated across all five sweep targets.
